title: Valencia Flash Flood Disaster 2024
daac: ASF DAAC / NASA PO.DAAC / NASA Earthdata (Verified OPERA SAR)
headline: 53.9 km² of verified flash flood extent mapped through torrential clouds using Sentinel-1 SAR.
story: On October 29–30, 2024, an isolated high-altitude depression (DANA) dumped over a year of precipitation in hours across the Valencian Community. Torrential flash floods breached drainage channels south of Valencia, submerging farmland, industrial suburbs, and coastal basins. While optical sensors were blinded by storm clouds, NASA OPERA Sentinel-1 SAR microwave pulses (5.405 GHz) penetrated the cloud deck directly, capturing the sudden +53.9 km² flood expansion via specular radar reflection.
why_sar: Why radar sees through cloud and night: Optical imagery was rendered completely unusable by the dense torrential storm clouds during the peak disaster hours, while radar passed straight through to map flooded neighborhoods.

story_steps.title: Pre-Event Coastal Plain
story_steps.description: Dry agricultural fields and urban settlements south of Valencia prior to the catastrophic DANA weather event.

story_steps.title: Post-Disaster Flash Flood Inundation
story_steps.description: Torrential waters filled river ravines and flooded surrounding plains, visibly dark in radar backscatter.

story_steps.title: OPERA DSWx-S1 Water Extent
story_steps.description: Algorithmic water classification isolates standing water bodies and agricultural drowning zones.

story_steps.title: Albufera Coastal Lagoon Expansion
story_steps.description: Massive sediment and stormwater runoff expanded the Albufera wetland complex before emptying into the Mediterranean.
